title: Family relationships and personal plans
instructionsHu: A vizsgáztató a családi kapcsolataidról, az otthoni életről és a jövőbeli terveidről kérdez. Válaszolj részletesen, fejtsd ki a véleményedet, és indokold példákkal.

questions.q: How would you describe the relationship between you and your parents?
followUps: Has it changed in the last few years? In what way?

questions.q: Which member of your family has influenced you the most? Why?
How are household chores shared in your family? Do you think it's fair?
Which family traditions are important to you, and why?
Do you think being an only child is an advantage or a disadvantage? Why?
How often do you spend quality time with your family, and what do you do together?
At what age do you think young people should move out of their parents' home? Why?
What do you think is the biggest challenge for families today?
followUps: How could families deal with it?

questions.q: Where do you see yourself in ten years' time?
Would you like to have a family like the one you grew up in? Why or why not?

usefulPhrases.en: We don't always see eye to eye.
She has been a role model for me.
It's only fair that everyone does their share.
usefulPhrases.hu: Csak az igazságos, ha mindenki kiveszi a részét.

usefulPhrases.en: One of the biggest challenges is ...
It has its pros and cons.
usefulPhrases.hu: Megvannak az előnyei és a hátrányai.

turns.speaker: examiner
turns.text: How would you describe the relationship between you and your parents?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: On the whole, it's pretty good. I can talk to my mum about almost anything, and my dad and I share a passion for football, so we often go to matches together.

turns.speaker: examiner
turns.text: Has it changed in the last few years? In what way?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Yes, it has. When I was about fourteen, we argued a lot about how late I could stay out, but now they trust me more, and I've become more understanding, too.

turns.speaker: examiner
turns.text: How are household chores shared in your family? Do you think it's fair?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: We've got a rota on the fridge: I do the washing-up and take out the rubbish, my sister does the hoovering, and my parents do the rest. It's reasonably fair, although my mum still ends up doing more than anyone else, which isn't really right.

turns.speaker: examiner
turns.text: Which family traditions are important to you, and why?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Christmas Eve, definitely. We always decorate the tree together and have fish soup, just like at my grandparents' house when my dad was a child. Traditions like that make me feel connected to the older generations.

turns.speaker: examiner
turns.text: At what age do you think young people should move out of their parents' home? Why?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: There's no perfect age, but I'd say in their mid-twenties, once they have a steady income. Living alone teaches you independence, but with rents being so high, I can understand why many people stay at home longer.

notes: Feladat teljesítése: a válaszok kifejtettek, a változásról szóló visszakérdezésre a vizsgázó múltbeli és jelenlegi példával felel, a költözés elvontabb kérdésénél pedig mérlegel, és megindokolja az álláspontját.

Nyelvhelyesség: B2-es szerkezetek hibátlanul – Present Perfect (I've become more understanding), az 'end up + -ing', a 'with rents being so high' igeneves szerkezet és a 'which isn't really right' mellékmondat.
Szókincs: a családi élet pontos kifejezései (rota, do the washing-up, do the hoovering, steady income), a magyar kulturális példa (szenteste, halászlé) pedig hitelessé teszi a választ.
Érdemes megtanulni: „On the whole”, „share a passion for”, „ends up doing more than anyone else”, „make me feel connected to”.
